DSP Pack D3: DTFS, DTFT and DTFT Properties (Lecture 5)

Why this matters in the exam: Sample Test 1 (20 marks, 50 min) only covered Weeks 1–4: sampling, signal operations, system properties and LTI convolution. Lecture 5 onwards has never been tested, so the final is the first time the DTFT can be examined. Expect short, multi-part calculation questions of 2–5 marks each, like the four-part Sample Test questions. Tutorial 4 shows the most likely types. Q1 asks for the DTFT of a finite, right-sided, left-sided or shifted sequence. Q2 asks for X(0), ∠X(0), ∫X dω, X(π) and ∫|X|² dω “without explicitly computing X(ω)”. Those shortcuts can earn quick marks in an open-book paper.

Scope: this pack covers L05 slides 1–26. The frequency response H(ω), the LCCDE-to-H(ω) step and pole-zero sketching (slides 27–35, T4 Q3–Q7) are in pack D4. T4 Q3–4 appear in the practice list here only because they use the eigenfunction and shift ideas from this pack.

1. The core ideas

1.1 Discrete-time Fourier series (DTFS): periodic signals (brief)

For a periodic x(n) with fundamental period and :

1.2 The DTFT: aperiodic, finite-energy signals

Item What it says Trap
Polar form : magnitude and phase spectrum A negative real value has phase , not 0 (T4 Q2(b)).
Convergence Guaranteed if (absolutely summable) or (finite energy) converges only for . has no DTFT. does (T4 Q1(b)).
Periodicity Always reduce to first, e.g.  and .
Parseval (energy) The integral equals energy, not the energy itself.

Why it is periodic: for integer . In sampling terms, a discrete-time signal has a periodic spectrum because sampling makes copies of every (section 1.6). Continuous-time signals have aperiodic spectra. Periodic signals have line spectra (DTFS). Aperiodic finite-energy signals have continuous spectra (DTFT).

1.6 The sampling theorem revisited (slides 13–16)

Sampling at gives:

  • Theorem: if for , then is recoverable when (the Nyquist rate is ). Recovery is by an ideal lowpass filter with gain and cutoff between and .
  • The gain cancels the in front of the replicas.

Frequency classes (slide 18): lowpass signals have energy near . Highpass signals have energy near . A signal cannot be both time-limited and bandlimited.

2. The method

Playbook A: “Compute the Fourier transform of x(n)” (T4 Q1)

Recognise it: a sequence is given and is asked for. Decide which case it is from the support of .

  1. Finite sequence (listed with ↑, or a pulse): write term by term. Use the ↑ to set each exponent. If the values are symmetric about some , factor out the centre exponent and use Euler to get cos/sin (T4 Q1(d)). A run of equal values is a finite geometric series: .
  2. Right-sided ( or ): check . Change variable so the sum starts at 0. Pull the constant outside. Then apply with (T4 Q1(c)).
  3. Left-sided (): substitute to get . This needs (T4 Q1(b)).
  4. Two-sided: split it into the part and the part. Do each part with step 2 or 3 and add the results. Do not count twice.
  5. Check: from your formula must equal . This takes 20 seconds and catches most errors.

  • Parseval factor. , not . For the inverse DTFT at , the integral is , not .
  • Geometric series off by one. has 6 terms (), so the numerator is , not .

  • Time expansion direction. compresses the spectrum. It is not . Watch for images at .
